description: Fideo Seco is a cherished Mexican dish featuring toasted short pasta cooked in a rich, savory tomato-based sauce until dry and flavorful. This comforting 'dry noodle' dish is a staple in many Mexican homes, often served as a side or a light main course. Its simplicity and deep flavors make it a beloved classic that's easy to prepare and always satisfying.

instructions.title: Prepare the Tomato Sauce Base
instructions.text: In a blender, combine the roughly chopped Roma tomatoes, 1/4 of a white onion, 2 peeled garlic cloves, and 1 cup of chicken broth. Blend until very smooth. Set aside.

instructions.title: Toast the Fideo Pasta
instructions.text: Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the broken fideo pasta and cook, stirring constantly, until golden brown. This step is crucial for flavor and texture. Be careful not to burn it.

instructions.title: Add the Sauce and Simmer
instructions.text: Carefully pour the blended tomato mixture into the skillet with the toasted fideo. Stir well to combine. It will sizzle. Add the remaining 2 cups of chicken broth and 1 teaspoon of salt. Bring the mixture to a boil.

instructions.title: Cook Until Liquid is Absorbed
instructions.text: Reduce the heat to low, cover the skillet, and let it simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the fideo is tender and most of the liquid has been absorbed. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Rest and Fluff
instructions.text: Once the fideo is cooked and the liquid is absorbed, remove the skillet from the heat. Keep it covered and let it rest for 5 minutes. This allows the pasta to fully absorb any remaining moisture and become perfectly tender.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Fluff the fideo seco with a fork. Serve hot, garnished generously with fresh chopped cilantro, a drizzle of Mexican crema, crumbled queso fresco, and slices of fresh avocado.

tips: Toasting the fideo pasta until deeply golden is key to its unique flavor and prevents it from becoming mushy. Keep a close eye on it as it can burn quickly.
For a vegetarian version, simply substitute chicken broth with vegetable broth. You can also add a pinch of cumin to the sauce for an extra layer of traditional Mexican flavor.
Fideo Seco is excellent served as a side dish with grilled meats or chicken, or as a light main course. Leftovers store well in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
